item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.content:encoded: Thank you for the feedback! I've updated the narrative a bit more to make it more cohesive, emphasizing the mystery, and also changed the symptoms of the SCP to make a bit more narrative sense.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.content:encoded:
I like the idea of there being a mysterious star exerting influence over humans, and then gradually learning that the star is intelligent and acting deliberately to some terrible end. On the other hand, the "Algernoning" effect you described doesn't really interest me at all. I think part of the reason is that the Algernonification is tied to the victims' respective professions in such a straightforward way. There's no intrigue when the outcome of an experiment is so predictable, and there's no impact in inflicting misery on a series of characters without having some degree of emotional buildup and payoff.

No greenlight from me I'm afraid, but I think the idea is worth revisiting and revising.

item.title: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Light horror

Elevator Pitch: A dim, distant star is discovered by a group of astronomers who discover that, when extensively gazed upon, said star can temporarily impart seemingly supernatural enhancements to the viewer. Said enhancements come at a price, however.

Central Narrative: A small research team in Argentina discovers a hitherto unknown star. The initial astronomer who extensively gazes at the star notes a small mote of light in the corner of his eye, though the light dissipates after several hours, since he chooses to ignore it. His partner, however, continues to be bothered by the light in the corner of her eye and keeps staring at it. Once she stares at it for an arbitrary amount of time, she abruptly begins collecting scrap metal around the site and feverishly attempting to build something. Attempts to communicate with her are ignored, and the few times she does speak, it's in an unrecognizable language. Her partner also notices that her scalera are bright yellow, as if jaundiced. This frenetic state lasts for about thirteen hours before abruptly ceasing, after which she has no memory of the experience and is left with symptoms similar to Parkinson's Disease.

SCP is made aware of this development and has its own team investigate the star, which has been designated Algernon-13 (after the novel "Flowers for Algernon"). Numerous D-class personnel undergo tests, and over the course of these tests, those subjected to viewing the mote of light seem to become "possessed" by something, though the possession varies. Two subjects experience increased strength and aggression, accompanied by red "bloodshot" eyes, as well as subsequent muscle atrophy once the episode has passed, while a third is calmer and able to communicate with SCP personnel by painting pictures to answer their questions, while the subject's scalerae have a purple tint to them; post experiment, they're struck blind and mute. The final experiment produces yet another result, accompanied by a dire warning.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook involves the mystery behind why the star induces "attribute enhancements" on its viewers. The mystery reaches its zenith with the pictures painted by the artist, as they give a nebulous picture of what's going on around the star, leaving one with as many new questions as answers.

Additional Notes: Not sure what to rate this anomaly - Euclid or Keter class. Suggestions would be helpful.
